done_when: On Windows, codex.identity reads a process's start time and executable path through the Windows API with ctypes (OpenProcess, GetProcessTimes, QueryFullProcessImageNameW) instead of running PowerShell, so no child process is started; identity keeps its contract (None when no process has the id, a matching record otherwise, and a reused id never matches); POSIX is unchanged; a test on Windows exercises a live process, an exited one and a mismatch

findings.body: This assertion now expects `it counts as held`, but the production message in `src/forge/codex.py:75` remains `it counts it as held`. Consequently, `test_5_one_worker_per_item` fails on Linux and macOS whenever it reaches this case. Restore the original expected text to preserve the unchanged POSIX behavior and keep CI passing.
findings.title: Restore the expected POSIX refusal message

findings.body: Returning the executable path also changes the driver's record for cold reads: `src/forge/codex.py:263–268` saves this identity directly. However, `tests/test_codex_reader.py:129` still unconditionally requires `codex_turn` in that record's command. On Windows the value is now the Python executable path, so `test_10_the_cold_read_runs_on_the_other_family` fails. This test runs in the Windows suite configured at `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23–36`. Update its assertion for the native Windows representation, as this branch already does for the worker test.
findings.title: Update the cold-reader test for Windows executable-path records

why: On Windows, Forge's process check (codex.identity) shells out to PowerShell Get-CimInstance, and CI shows that call sometimes never returns: a pytest worker hung in subprocess communicate() during crash recovery (test_codex_resume.py test_9), like the earlier Windows hang in test_4
